full_judgment: 3. First information report was lodged on 21-9-2001 of an occurrence dated 20-9-2001 occurred at 11-00 PM and in this first information report, the name of accused petitioners appeared as accused Nos. 1 and 4. This first information report was lodged under sections 143/341/307/332 of the Penal Code and under section 3/4 of Explosive Substance Act. From narration of facts in the first information report it appears that in the election campaign, the informant was subjected to bomb explosion. At that time by the light of the car the informant could recognise the accused petitioners with co-accuseds taking active part in hurling bombs. This case was investigated by Bhola Police Station and there being a prima facie case found against the accuseds, charge sheet was submitted on 21-5-2005 against the accused petitioners and co-accuseds. Thereafter the case was sent to Additional District Magistrate and from the order sheet it appears that the learned Magistrate received the first information report and it also appears that some of the accused appeared and were enlarged on bail. The accused petitioner appeared before this Court and obtained anticipatory bail from this Court. From the order dated 5-3-2002 it appears that the learned Magistrate passed the following order এজাহার ভূক্ত আসামী আঃ অদুদ মেম্বার এর জামিন না মঞ্জুর হইয়া হাজতে প্রেরণের আদেশ আছে” The bail application filed by the accused petitioner, A. Wadud Member, was rejected by the Sessions Judge in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.2126 of 2002 but it appears from order dated 14-3-2002, that the accused petitioner obtained anticipatory bail from this Court. The relevant portion of the said order runs as follows: অত্র মামলার হাজতী আঃ অদুদ এর আগাম জামিনের ইং ১৯-২-২০০২ তাং আদেশের অনুলিপি পাওয়া গেল” When the bail of the accused petitioner was rejected by the Sessions Judge, and the accused-petitioner was in custody, it is very unfortunate that suppressing the said facts, the accused petitioner A. Wadud obtained anticipatory bail from this Court. Here, it may be pointed out that at the time of granting anticipatory bail, it is the requirement of law that the accused must be present before the Court and the court being satisfied that accused is not fugitive from justice, can grant anticipatory bail. From the facts disclosed by the petitioners and appears from the order sheet annexed with the Rule petition, it appears that when the anticipatory bail was granted, the accused petitioner was in custody and either a false person was presented before the court or the petitioner suppressed the true facts or this court without knowing the implication of anticipatory bail, granted the same. But whatever the case may be, it is very unfortunate. When accused is in custody the accused is not entitled for anticipatory bail, a bail may be granted. From the aforesaid facts the conduct of the accused petitioner is totally exposed as he has a habit of concealing the true fact before the Court. It appears the learned Magistrate framed charge in this case on 8-2-2004 under sections 143/341/323/307 of the Penal Code. It also appears that case has been transferred to the Court of Additional District Magistrate for trial. After long 2 years of framing of charge the accused petitioner moved this Court and obtained this Rule.
